def: Portable Document Format, a file format that stores instructions for painting pages so they look identical everywhere, not the logical structure of the document.
A language that describes what to draw and where on a page, such as the operators in a PDF content stream, rather than the document's paragraphs and headings.
The compressed sequence of drawing operators for one PDF page, which holds all of the page's text as strings with coordinates.
A PDF produced by software from a digital source, containing real text operators and usually an accurate text layer.
A PDF whose pages are images of paper and which contains no characters unless an OCR text layer has been added.
Text positioned over a page image with render mode 3 so that it can be searched and copied but is not painted, usually the output of an earlier OCR run.
A table in a PDF font that says which Unicode character each glyph code stands for; without it, extracted text may be gibberish.
Turning a page into typed blocks such as titles, paragraphs, tables, figures, captions, headers and footers.
A dataset of 80,863 human-annotated document pages with bounding boxes in 11 layout classes, widely used to train layout detectors.
The sequence in which a person would read the blocks of a page, which differs from the order in which they are stored in the file.
A top-down reading-order method that repeatedly splits a page on its widest horizontal or vertical band of whitespace and recurses on the parts.
A stored description of one layout block with its page, bounding box, type, reading-order position and the source of its text.
